LSCH.name: Gentle Starter
LSCH.catch: Light, gentle, and gone in a breath
LSCH.desc: “Clean” and “easy to drink” are the best compliments you can give. Start with low-fuss beers that carry just a whisper of hop freshness and you can’t go wrong.
LSCH.hint: Just ask for “the easiest-drinking beer you have.” That’s the right move.

LSAH.name: Fruity Hunter
LSAH.catch: Light on its feet, chasing aroma
LSAH.desc: You like a light body, but you want the aroma to be bold. You enjoy citrusy, tropical hop aromas almost like juice.
LSAH.hint: Spot the words “session”, “XPA” or “citrus” on a tap and don’t hesitate.

LBCH.name: Crisp Master
LBCH.desc: No frills, all about the crispness. A lager with restrained aroma and a sharp streak of bitterness may actually be your true favourite.
LBCH.hint: Look for a “pilsner” or “lager” tap and get it well chilled.

LBAH.name: Hop Rocker
LBAH.catch: Light body, aroma and bitterness turned all the way up
LBAH.desc: A light body with hop aroma and bitterness hitting hard on top. You like the thrill of a live show and want to taste the hops themselves.
LBAH.hint: Keep an eye out for “fresh hop” and “pale ale” taps.

LSCM.name: Mellow Collector
LSCM.desc: You want to quietly savour the gentle sweetness of malt. You collect unpretentious flavours and find real value in a beer you could drink every day.
LSCM.hint: Start with gentle golden beers such as a Helles or a Dortmunder.

LSAM.name: Soft Aromatist
LSAM.catch: A sweet aroma that drifts out softly
LSAM.desc: You love the soft banana and citrus notes that malt and yeast create. The hops stay quiet while the aroma blooms. Wheat beers are made for you.
LSAM.hint: Look for “Weizen”, “Wit” or “wheat” on the tap list.

LBCM.name: Afterglow Keeper
LBCM.desc: It looks black, yet it drinks surprisingly light. You quietly guard the coffee-like roasted bitterness and the finish that fades away in a breath.
LBCM.hint: Ask: “Do you have something dark but light?”

LBAM.name: Flavor Tuner
LBAM.catch: Character in the aroma, a dry finish
LBAM.desc: Strong in both bitterness and aroma, but the source isn’t hops. You can pick out herbs, smoke and yeast character, and tune them to your own taste.
LBAM.hint: Keep an eye out for “saison”, “spice” and “smoke” taps.

FSCH.name: Rich Relaxer
FSCH.desc: Plenty of substance, but a calm aroma. You like to unwind slowly with a classic beer where malt and hops are in balance.
FSCH.hint: Go for reddish-brown beers such as an “amber” or a “red”.

FSAH.name: Juicy Collector
FSAH.catch: Thick and rich, with an orchard of aroma
FSAH.desc: A rich mouthfeel with tropical aromas swirling through it. This is the hottest direction right now, and you want to collect the aroma of every single glass.

FBCH.name: Classic Bitter
FBCH.desc: You like sturdy beers that come at you with bitterness rather than aroma. Unmoved by trends, you savour a classic IPA at your own pace.
FBCH.hint: Among the IPAs, pick a “West Coast” or a “dry” one.

FBAH.name: Hop Swordmaster
FBAH.desc: Aroma, bitterness and body all at maximum. You can take a punchy, hop-loaded beer head on.

FSCM.name: Malt Philosopher
FSCM.desc: You like classic, full-bodied beers with a thick spread of malt sweetness. Depth over flash. You read the story of the malt in every glass.
FSCM.hint: “Bock” and “Scotch” are proof of rich malt sweetness.

FSAM.name: Malt Dandy
FSAM.desc: Heavy, sweet and richly aromatic. A gentleman who enjoys dense beers with notes of dried fruit and caramel, with plenty of poise.
FSAM.hint: These are often strong, so try several in small sizes.

FBCM.name: Dark Meister
FBCM.catch: Roastiness and bitterness seal the deal
FBCM.desc: The deep bitterness of roasted malt and a heavy body are what win you over. You wear quiet, smoky dark beers as naturally as a suit.

FBAM.name: Craft Legend
FBAM.catch: Heavy and bold, for the last beer of the night
FBAM.desc: You take on the intense aroma and bitterness of roast and smoke, all of it. You live at the deepest point of the craft beer rabbit hole, and barrel-aged or imperial beers suit you best.
FBAM.hint: If you find “imperial”, “barrel” or “rauch”, it’s worth trying even if you have to share.

1.pr: A soft lager brewed to celebrate the birth of Princess Aiko. Gentle in aroma and flavour, and very easy to drink.
1.aroma: An elegant aroma reminiscent of goyo-tsutsuji (five-leaf azalea).
1.pour: Pilsner glass, 7°C. Start with the foam, then pour slowly.
1.story: A completely unfiltered, unpasteurised craft beer brewed with pure snowmelt water from the Nasu mountains and carefully selected ingredients, packed with love for Nasu.
1.trivia:
Nasu Kohgen Beer Ai was brewed with a special recipe to celebrate the birth of Princess Aiko.
The label shows the goyo-tsutsuji azalea, her personal emblem.
The emblem was chosen, we hear, from the azaleas blooming at the imperial villa in Nasu, with the wish that she would grow up as pure and gentle as the flower.
Our motto has been to brew with love and happiness folded into every delicious drop.
The beautiful name given to Princess Aiko was one of the things that inspired this beer.

2.pr: Part of our “FARM TO YOU” series using ingredients from our home prefecture of Akita, brewed generously with hops from Yokote. Hop character reminiscent of tropical fruit, citrus and grapefruit. A fruity, intense hop aroma with solid bitterness.
2.aroma: Tropical notes of mango and pineapple with a citrus edge of grapefruit and orange. Bold hop aroma and solid bitterness.
2.pour: Slightly warmer at 10°C, in a glass that lifts the aroma.
2.story: A craft beer and hard cider brewery born in 2023 inside a renovated bathhouse, the last public bath in Akita City. We brew with hops from Yokote, one of Japan’s leading hop regions, and fruit from Akita!
2.region: A small brewery born from the renovation of Hoshi-no-yu, the last public bathhouse in Akita City. Akita is actually one of Japan’s top hop-growing prefectures, and apples are grown widely too. We use local hops and Akita fruit to share flavours you can only find here.
2.trivia: The bathhouse closed in 2021, but once or twice a month someone still walks in asking “Is the bath open today?”. Locals still seem to remember us as the bathhouse.

3.pr: Hazy in appearance, with bold hop aroma and the juicy flavour of dried persimmon. If more bears start showing up around Inami, blame this beer and its persimmons.
3.aroma: Fruity hop aroma leads the way
3.story: “Indigenous brewing.” With the skills of a former winemaker and small-batch brewing, we aim to co-create beers that let you feel the terroir: the culture that is born only from this land and these people. Let’s drink up everything the land gives us! “The ecosystem of the land. Conversation between people. And in between, there is beer!” We bring plenty of homegrown beer from Inami, Nanto. Cheers!
3.region: KUMA MASSIGURA uses dried persimmon, a local speciality, making use of blemished fruit that can’t be sold. Processed goods like these are subject to production limits set by the cooperative, so even in a bumper year the shipment volume is fixed, and more and more fruit goes unsold even after being dried. The result is persimmons left to ripen on the tree, drawing bears and other wildlife preparing for hibernation into the orchards and causing damage for residents. We ask farmers to ship the good fruit to the cooperative while NAT.BREW buys the blemished fruit under contract, hoping to help solve a local problem, even a little.
3.trivia: The dried persimmons are boiled with the wort. We brew so that the fruity hop aroma stays central while the sweetness and distinctive thickness of the persimmon come through in the beer.

4.pr: Brewed with green Sichuan pepper. A sharp tingle and a fresh mandarin-like aroma with a clean finish. Our most popular beer, and it goes with any dish.
4.aroma: A strong green Sichuan pepper aroma that brings mapo tofu to mind
4.pour: Tulip glass at around 8°C. Enjoy the aroma as you drink.
4.story: Romeo Brewery is a brewpub right under Tokyo Skytree. We brew richly aromatic, distinctive beers that make the most of herbs and spices. We care about the food too: our spiced meat dishes and seasonal pasta are highly recommended. In the bustle of the city, we aim to be a space where the scent of herbs puts your mind at ease.
4.trivia: The owner is a University of Tsukuba graduate, so this beer festival is a highlight every year. Come and say hello!

5.pr: An IPA that flies free like a migrating bird. Bold citrus aroma and rich bitterness invite you on a pleasant journey.
5.aroma: Notes of pink grapefruit and guava
5.story: Beer and wine, both. Carrying that name, we compromise on neither. Through trial and error we keep chasing “delicious” with sincerity. We polish both crafts in earnest to deliver a glass that brings a smile with every sip. Come and experience our two-way craft at the festival.
5.region:
In Ushiku, Ibaraki, we make our drinks while honouring the history and character of the region.
In this town, where the history of Japanese wine lives on, we tend our own vineyard and are working to revive Ushiku wine.
Through drinks that use local produce and by taking part in events inside and outside the prefecture,
we widen our circle of friends and share the appeal of Ushiku one glass at a time.

6.pr: A jalapeño beer with a curious kick. Layering refined heat and just the right jalapeño aroma onto beer is no easy feat, but DD4D’s craftsmanship adds an exquisite edge. Fresh jalapeño flavour meets hop bitterness and tropical aroma in an addictive jalapeño IPA.
6.aroma: Enjoy the harmony of fresh, green jalapeño and citrusy hop aroma.
6.food: Fried chicken, fries, burgers, sausages, meat, spicy food
6.pour: Pint glass with a small head.
6.story: DD4D opened in Matsuyama in 1998 as a select shop. Driven by the founder’s belief in “ignoring convention and following the path you believe in”, a craft brewery was completed inside the Chifune-cho store in 2019, and it was reborn as DD4D BREWING & CLOTHING STORE. In 2021 a second brewery opened in the nearby port town of Mitsuhama. Over 300 beers sold nationwide and overseas so far, with many collaborations across sport, apparel, confectionery, film and more.
6.region: Our beers use plenty of ingredients from our home prefecture of Ehime. We don’t insist on local sourcing for its own sake, but we are lucky to be surrounded by wonderful ingredients that suit beer. Beyond the classic iyokan and kawachi bankan citrus, we have used jalapeños, naked barley, and salt and sake yeast from collaborations with local companies. The connections beer creates keep turning into new excitement beyond anything we imagined.
6.trivia: Our team comes from overseas and from all over Japan. Each member brings their own experience, knowledge and passion, and that is what creates DD4D’s distinctive beers and everything around them. By the way, the beer business started in 2019, but the shop has a much longer history as an apparel store, going back to 1998.

7.pr: Noble hop aroma with restrained hop bitterness. A straw-coloured, clean-bodied beer with a fresh, fruity aroma.
7.aroma: A fruity aroma reminiscent of fresh fruit, with noble hops in the background
7.story: Founded in 1998. In a brewery of barely 65 square metres we make a wide range of beers. Under the motto “Small Brewery, Big Beer” we brew styles from around the world, from the cutting edge to beers that have long since died out. In our 28th year, we keep taking on new beers.
7.region: The only brewery in Sakura City.

8.pr: A fruit ale inspired by Himeji Castle, the World Heritage site, made with yuzu and sansho pepper harvested in Hyogo. To bring out the full aroma of yuzu grown among beautiful mountains and clear water, we use plenty of yuzu peel and juice for a juicy, easy-drinking beer that shows yuzu at its best.
8.aroma: Bold yuzu aroma with the fruitiness of Belgian yeast.
8.story: Free Spirits Brewing started brewing in Himeji, Hyogo in October 2022. “Free spirits” means doing things your own way, and our motto is to brew without being bound by fixed ideas. We will do our best to make the event a great one through craft beer. Cheers!
8.region: Our flagship White Castle Ale is a fruit beer made with yuzu harvested in Yasutomi, Himeji and nearby. Himeji is known for yuzu, and we use locally grown fruit with local revitalisation in mind. With depopulation and ageing leaving the countryside short of hands for the harvest, we also lead small groups of volunteers to help pick the yuzu.
8.trivia:
Few people know how dangerous yuzu harvesting is: the thorns are serious.
Helmets, safety glasses and thick gloves are a must. We had no idea on our first harvest and had to borrow all the gear from the farmers.

9.pr: A South German wheat ale with banana-like aroma, gentle sweetness and a smooth mouthfeel.
9.pour: Weizen glass, 8°C. Needs a proper head; the yeast haze is part of the style.
9.story: Twin Peaks Mountain Brewing in Tsukuba, Ibaraki takes its name from Mount Tsukuba and its twin peaks. Our German brewer makes authentic German beer under the German purity law, using only water, malt, hops and yeast with no additives at all. You can taste the passion in the brewing and the generous use of quality ingredients. We import raw materials from the homeland of each style we aim for and brew authentic German-style craft beer fresh. We also make other delicious styles beyond Germany, so craft beer lovers can enjoy a varied range of German and international flavours.
9.region: We use soft water from Lake Kasumigaura. Soft water is ideal for brewing because it suits many beer styles and creates delicious flavour.
9.trivia: Because the craft beer movement started in the USA, many people assume German beer can’t be craft beer. But craft beer is defined by three things: handmade, small-scale and independent. So Twin Peaks Mountain Brewing doesn’t just specialise in German styles; it brews true craft beer.

10.location: Shizuoka (Kambara-juku on the old Tokaido road)
10.pr: A sake brewery-approved series: we visit sake breweries and turn their sake lees into the finest beer. Gold medal at the International Beer Cup, Japanese craft recognised by the world.
10.aroma: A gentle note of Shizuoka Beni-hoppe strawberries as a hidden touch, with the rich flavour of sake lees.
10.pour: Around 5°C, with a light head, in any glass you like.
10.story: A brewery based in Kambara-juku, the 15th post town on the old Tokaido road at the foot of Mt Fuji. Drawing on the gifts of Shizuoka’s mild mountains and sea, our brewer, a data scientist, uses sensors fitted to the equipment to brew by the numbers. While respecting traditional methods, we keep creating new beers that break the mould, such as our hugely popular Sake Kasu IPA. Winner of many awards at national and international competitions. Come and try a glass we are proud of.
10.region: Our beers are served at local restaurants too, and we hear the sake lees series is especially popular with local customers.
10.trivia: Unlike amazake, the beer keeps its natural drinkability while we treasure the flavour and mellowness that come from the sake lees.

11.pr: One sip, and you’re on the walk home at sunset. The aroma of Earl Grey and a faint sweetness make an ordinary moment a little richer.
11.aroma: Earl Grey, through and through. You won’t need to search for it.
11.pour: Pour quietly down the side of the glass. The colder, the better.
11.story: Craft beer born in Kamiooka, Yokohama. To grow the craft beer community, we brew a wide variety of styles that go beyond existing beers.
11.region: We are on good terms with the local Keikyu railway and the Keikyu department store.
11.trivia:
In August we made a tomato beer in collaboration with a local tomato farmer.
It debuted at the beer festival held at Keikyu Department Store in September.

12.pr: Grapefruit citrus and a rich, full mouthfeel
12.story: A beer that makes punk rockers grin. We are the largest farm in Fukushima City. Beyond every toast, the future of farming.
12.region: Beer made by rice farmers in a brewery surrounded by fields
12.trivia: A beer we have kept refining bit by bit since the early days of brewing

13.pr: A sour ale made with Koshu, a white wine grape. Like a lighter sparkling wine: no sweetness, no bitterness, just a clean taste.
13.food: Anything that goes with champagne: strawberry shortcake, prosciutto and so on.
13.pour: A wine glass if you are taking your time. Well chilled, no head.
13.story: In Koshu, Yamanashi, we specialise in just two styles: sours fermented with lactic acid bacteria, and stouts. Yamanashi is a kingdom of fruit, famous for grapes, peaches and strawberries, and fruit goes wonderfully with sours. Adding herbs and spices gives complexity while keeping the taste clean. Fruit beers are often expected to be sweet, but we add the fruit before fermentation so the yeast consumes the sugar, leaving no sweetness behind.
13.region:
The grapes we use are harvested near the brewery. This area, the Kyoto district, was recognised in 2022 as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System for its “fruit farming system adapted to the alluvial fans”.
A local company turns the grapes into purée so we can brew with them all year round.
13.trivia:
1. Why the beer isn’t sweet even though it uses fruit: we add it before fermentation, so the yeast eats up all the sugar.
2. Why the sour isn’t bitter even though it is beer: no hops.
Hops add strong bitterness and aroma that would get in the way of the delicate fruit aroma.

14.pr: A “Green Room” is the magical moment inside the tunnel of a wave when light through the seawater turns everything green. This pale gold, clear beer packed with refreshing hop aroma and flavour brings that Green Room to mind.
14.aroma: A fresh green note like white wine, with grapefruit-like citrus
14.pour: Pint glass, start drinking at around 4°C
14.story: We opened our brewery and taproom in 2025 in Shimoda, at the southern tip of the Izu Peninsula. Our brewing team, with over ten years of experience, is committed to delivering the highest-quality beer. This place has breathtaking blue sea and sandy beaches, and we are always asking what beer we would want to drink here. If you like our beer even a little, we hope you will come to this beautiful, nostalgic town, soak in its slow pace of time, and drink a beer just for the sake of it. We always have beer ready for that. Shimoda Brewing is run by Two Dogs Taproom in Roppongi, Tokyo, where you can enjoy 20 taps of Japanese and international beer, always including around six of ours.
14.region: Our Shimoda Lager is made with 100% Japanese malt, bought from Sato Malting in Ishioka, Ibaraki. To source all of that barley from Shimoda itself, we have started a project to use abandoned farmland in the area. This year, with help from locals, we brewed an experimental batch of Shimoda Lager with 80 kg of Shimoda-grown malt.
14.trivia: Our main venue is Two Dogs Taproom in Roppongi, where Shimoda Brewing beer is always on tap. There is also Shimoda Brewing Ikebukuro, where you can enjoy wood-fired pizza with our beer.

15.pr: Made only with aromatic hops grown in Tamura. An adventurous fresh hop series that changes its aroma hop with every batch.
15.aroma: The fresh, lively aroma only fresh hops can give. Each batch uses a different hop, so every aroma is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter.
15.food: Fish and chips, Caesar salad and the like
15.story: A brewery in Miyakoji, Tamura, Fukushima that grows its own hops. We started brewing in 2020 and are now in our sixth year. What makes us special is that we brew with our own fresh hops all year round. Abukuma GREEN (Fresh hop IPA) in particular changes its aroma hop with every monthly batch, so the hop flavour differs depending on when you drink it. Come and enjoy the fresh aroma and taste of fresh hops at the festival!
15.region:
Besides fresh hop beers made with locally grown hops, we brew limited-edition beers with fruit and vegetables from Fukushima,
and special collaboration beers with wineries, sake breweries and distilleries in the prefecture.
Through camping and other outdoor experiences, sport, hands-on learning and hop harvesting, we are a brewery where many people meet and connect.
15.trivia: We are Hop Japan, a craft brewery in Tamura, Fukushima that handles everything from growing our own hops to brewing. Our signature feature is a year-round lineup brewed with fresh hops. From fresh hop beers to fruit beers and barrel-aged beers, we brew a wide range of styles. Next to the brewery we also run a campsite and lodges, so you can enjoy craft beer surrounded by mountains and nature. At the festival we will have a lineup for everyone from beer beginners to seasoned fans, so please drop by! Cheers!!

16.pr: A beer that puts the quality of Honjo’s hard water front and centre. Citrus in the aroma, a solid body and a dry finish.
16.aroma: Citrus aroma in harmony with toasty malt aroma
16.pour: A straight-sided glass, around 7°C, best with no head.
16.story: We are Honjo Ginza Brewery from Honjo, Saitama! Coming to Tsukuba has become a yearly tradition. This year too we are bringing plenty of beers that are full-bodied yet crisp, perfect for Tsukuba! Our beer quality keeps levelling up every year. With the festival held in autumn this time, we are also bringing beers perfect for the season. Let’s make it a great one!
16.region: We brew with the hard water of Honjo, where our brewery is located
16.trivia: Our brewery and attached taproom are a six-minute walk from JR Honjo Station. Homely atmosphere, plus plenty of food such as pasta and ajillo. After drinking our beer in Tsukuba, come and visit the taproom!

17.pr: No regular lineup since day one! Sometimes matching the times and the scene, sometimes not, BLUE MAGIC brews limited beers for the event where we want you to drink them, right then.
17.aroma: Your nose is a fine one for finding a beer this rare, a once-in-a-lifetime encounter
17.pour: No head, so the aroma and flavour hit you directly
17.story: After a few years away… the blue frog is back at TCBF! BLUE MAGIC is a brewpub in the heart of Utsunomiya, making everything from orthodox styles to one-of-a-kind beers born from wild ideas. Beers that go unrecorded but never forgotten, with a creativity you will only find here, at events like this! We will have a lineup that changes every day across the three days. The blue frog might just change your idea of beer!? Let’s raise a glass together in Tsukuba!!

18.pr: Made with rare Japanese peat: the beer “whisky makers fear”. Come and experience it!
18.aroma: The height of individuality. This is Smoke Craft at its purest.
18.pour: Like any beer: well chilled, please.
18.story: Smoke Craft throws down the gauntlet to the craft beer world with the sharpest techniques around. A brewery dedicated to smoked beer, leading the smoked beer scene worldwide. Many people have never tried a smoked beer, yet most of ours are competition winners. Our newest beer uses Japanese peat and is called, fittingly, Off Peat. The number of people hooked on this “almost whisky-like” beer is exploding.
18.region: The spent grain from brewing goes to local farmers, who use it as fertiliser, creating a sustainable production cycle.

19.company: Daichi to Umi no Campanella Brewing Co., Ltd.
19.pr: Made with 100% malt from “Barley of Hope” grown in Higashimatsushima. Enjoy the rich malt flavour.
19.aroma: The gentle herbal aroma of Tettnang, a German noble hop, with malt flavour.
19.story:
We started our brewery in Higashimatsushima, Miyagi in January 2025. We make craft beer with local primary produce, starting with “Barley of Hope”, grown on land recovered after the disaster.
Higashimatsushima is a small town of 38,000 people in the Ishinomaki area of Miyagi.
Around 80% of the land is farmland used for rice, and with the sea and two major rivers meeting at a fishing port, oyster and nori farming thrive in the nutrient-rich waters.
Yet with no processors or farm shops for either produce or seafood, we felt these wonderful primary products were going unknown.
We started a craft brewery believing that a processed, enjoyable product could be a way for more people to discover Higashimatsushima.
Our concept is “make what can only be made in Higashimatsushima”.
We believe things grown in the same climate go well together, so we aim for beer that pairs not just with local ingredients but with the culture, scenery and people of Higashimatsushima.
Among the many craft beers out there, ours may not be the very best.
But we promise it becomes the best beer when you drink it in Higashimatsushima.
We hope it gives you a reason to visit.
This is our first time at Tsukuba Craft Beer Fest. Cheers!
19.region:
Our two-row barley, the main ingredient, is grown by three farming corporations.
About 10 hectares are planted, yielding close to 50 tonnes a year.
Spent grain from brewing goes back to their rice fields as fertiliser.
Off-spec barley not fit for brewing is also recycled locally as a beer adjunct or as feed.
19.trivia:
■ “Barley of Hope”, born from land recovered after the disaster
In rice fields damaged by salt after the Great East Japan Earthquake, the whole community took up growing salt-tolerant two-row barley. Trial cultivation began in 2013, and together with farming corporations we worked out the growing methods and varieties suited to this land, settling on the Tochigi variety Sachiho Golden sown in autumn. Two-row barley dislikes the cold and the early harvests fell far short of those in Kanto or Kyushu. Thanks to the ingenuity of farmers who know this climate well, the harvest has grown to over 50 tonnes a year and is now used in craft whisky as well. Japanese barley is rarely used in craft beer, but raising the value of rotation crops helps stabilise farm businesses. Higashimatsushima is working on “sixth-sector” industry as a whole community.
The city was created in 2005 by merging the towns of Yamoto and Naruse, and even twenty years on, people identify more with their district than with the city. So rather than promoting the city as a whole, we plan to release a beer for each district, putting the spotlight on the producers working hard in each one.
We are casting the craftspeople who keep making good things despite the climate changes since the disaster as the twelve gods of Greek mythology.
Four are in production so far:
Demeter ⇒ Higashimatsushima Dortmunder, 100% Barley of Hope
Hera ⇒ Nobiru Weiss, with wheat from Agreed Naruse in Nobiru
Athena ⇒ Yamoto Pale Ale, with rice from Meguito in Yamoto
Poseidon ⇒ Otsuka Oyster Stout, with oysters from Goto Suisan in Otsuka
In the end there will be twelve gods: eight districts plus four seasonal beers.

20.pr: An IPA with the fresh aroma of Okinawan shikuwasa citrus. The refreshing bitterness from the juice brings the emerald-blue sea of Kumejima to mind.
20.aroma: Fresh citrus aroma from shikuwasa and hops.
20.story: Brewery Tumugi is the first craft brewery on Kumejima. Kumejima tsumugi silk is the island’s important intangible cultural asset. Like that silk, woven with heart, we want to make beer with care that weaves people together. That wish is in every glass.
20.region: Spent grain from brewing goes to a nearby cattle farmer, and the cattle raised on it are served in restaurants as “Kumejima beef steak”.
20.trivia:
Our brewer, Shimabukuro, is originally from Ibaraki and was featured on the TV programme “Gutto! Chikyu-bin”, which delivers parcels from parents back home.
https://www.ytv.co.jp/chikyubin/oa/article20241201.html

21.pr: As the name says, a HAZY IPA with an impactful hop aroma. Dry-hopped with a huge dose of four hops led by Mosaic! Enjoy the rich aroma and a fruity flavour that lives up to it!
21.story: In 2019 we built a brewery in Hanamaki, Iwate with our own hands and started brewing. We named it BrewBeast with the wish to create the best times (best and story) for everyone through brewing craft beer. New energy for the region through craft beer, and a “cool countryside” for Hanamaki.
21.region:
We run a taproom next to the brewery for local customers to enjoy.
Many collaboration beers with local companies too, from a lens maker to a custom car shop and the airport, spreading Hanamaki’s appeal within the city and beyond.
A second brewery is planned in central Hanamaki, with a park alongside, which we hope will become a place for locals to gather.
21.trivia:
When our founder Takahashi started the craft beer business, he had never actually drunk a craft beer (he loves it now).
The taproom next to the brewery, “Lit work place”, was renovated by Takahashi himself, a keen DIYer. He built most of the brewery too.
Other brewers and beer bar folk often visit Hanamaki for collaborations and events. Even with a brew day the next morning, the drinking goes late into the night, and there are Hanamaki tours by day.

22.pr: Grapefruit-like citrus comes first, followed by a soft aroma of peach and mango. The name comes from Konjiki-hime, the golden princess of Kokage Shrine in Tsukuba.
22.aroma: Grapefruit-like aroma at first, followed by rich fruit notes reminiscent of peach and mango
22.food: Juicy meat dishes of all kinds
22.pour: IPA glass at around 5°C. The aroma opens up even as it warms a little.
22.story:
The only brewery in Tsukuba, Ibaraki brewing with natural water from Mount Tsukuba.
In pursuit of the happiest glass, we use Mount Tsukuba spring water and Ibaraki malt,
taking on beers that are truly Tsukuba, day after day.
Each one made with heart.
Beer that connects people.
22.region:
For six years, 100% of our spent grain has gone to feed chickens and wild boar, with nothing wasted, in a sustainable cycle.
We also work with farmers growing Ibaraki barley and wheat, and brew with Ibaraki-grown grain.
We make beers with Tsukuba specialities such as Hitachi Oda rice and Fukure mikan and other fruit.
Through beer, we work to be a place that spreads the word about Tsukuba.
22.trivia:
Our red food truck is on the road!
The only craft beer in Tsukuba brewed with natural water from Mount Tsukuba.

23.pr: The flagship of “Nasu Desu Na”, brewed in a style that originated in England. An exquisite balance of hop aroma and bitterness with a clean, easy-drinking taste.
23.aroma: A crisp pale ale. Clean and easy to drink
23.pour: Well chilled, in a chilled glass. Head as you like it.
23.story: The charm of Nasu Desu Na. We brew easy-drinking, delicious beers with water from the foot of the Nasu mountains. Our limited series with more craft character is popular with seasoned fans too. We also make one of Japan’s few beers using whey (from Nasushiobara). Our many beer competition awards back up the taste and quality. Lastly, we will keep working toward our goal of spreading “Nasu Desu Na” as the word for cheers.
23.region: A certified Nasushiobara City brand business.
23.trivia:
Our whey protein beer is a collaboration with Senbonmatsu Farm, a certified Nasushiobara brand business, using their whey.
The label has a cow-print pattern, and one of the patches is shaped like a map of Nasushiobara.
The cow in our logo is there because Nasu means cows: Nasushiobara is the biggest raw milk producer on Honshu, and the city mascot is a cow.
The two humps on its back represent the Nasu mountains (Chausu-dake and Asahi-dake).
The bottle is a special twelve-sided one, its shoulders shaped to match the horns of the logo.

24.pr: A rare Japanese smoked beer made with malt we smoke ourselves at our smokehouse, with a smoky flavour that fills your mouth.
24.aroma: Smoky aroma from our house-smoked malt, smoked over beech.
24.pour: Tulip glass, around 10°C, with a generous head
24.story: NAMACHAん Brewing is a craft brewery that started brewing in Toshima, Tokyo in 2018. Based in Toshima, we have brewed beer rooted in the local community. With our new brewery we can now can our beer and deliver NAMACHAん beer across Japan. Our motto is “delicious beer with a little surprise”. From smoked beers to playful beers with fruit and spices, we brew something new every day. We are delighted you can enjoy them at this event! We have a lineup that beginners will enjoy too, so come and say hello 🍻
24.region:
As the first brewery in Toshima, Tokyo, we have been supported by the local community since we started brewing. We make collaboration beers with local shops and companies and take part in local festivals.
Many of our taproom regulars live nearby, some visiting several times a week, so we create more than five new beers a month to keep them happy.
24.trivia:
The rauchbier we are bringing is a smoked beer that originated in Germany, and we think very few breweries in Japan make one.
It is brewed with smoked malt, and since we do the smoking ourselves, it has a wonderfully pronounced smoky aroma.

25.pr: Made generously with mikan citrus harvested in Numazu, Shizuoka. The fresh mikan aroma and the fruity, spicy character of a saison come together in a clean taste. Enjoy Uchiura Saison, available only this season!
25.aroma: Fresh, juicy and richly sweet in aroma. Fresh mikan citrus in harmony with the spiciness typical of a saison.
25.food: Fried food such as fried chicken, of course, but also tangy snacks such as salmon carpaccio.
25.pour: Pour at 4°C, taking care not to lose the carbonation.
25.story:
ONE DROP is a craft brewery in Numazu, Shizuoka.
What we value most is creating moments where people connect with each other, and with the region, naturally through beer.
We brew approachable beers you never tire of, so that craft beer experts and newcomers alike find them delicious and fun.
We also put energy into beers that draw on the ingredients, culture and scenery of Numazu and Shizuoka.
Using local fruit and ingredients that come from connections with local businesses, we aim for a glass that lets you feel the air and background of the place, not just the taste.
This TCBF is ONE DROP’s first time at the festival.
We have beers ready that show the character of Numazu and Shizuoka, and the easy-drinking fun that is ONE DROP.
Enjoy a glass of ONE DROP at the festival.
25.region:
At ONE DROP, we value sharing the appeal of Shizuoka and Numazu through beer.
Our featured beer, Uchiura Saison, is made with seasonal mikan harvested in Numazu and Shizuoka.
We aim for a beer that captures the aroma and taste of mikan in season, and with it the scenery and feel of the season.
We have also taken on beers using unused ingredients from local inns and a collaboration with Awashima Marine Park, the aquarium in Numazu.
Our restaurant even has a space where you can enjoy craft beer while watching the penguins from Awashima Marine Park.
We hope to be a reason for people to take an interest in the town of Numazu, through beer.
25.trivia: Our restaurant has a penguin tank, and the penguins are adorable; you can even feed them. Craft beer with cute penguins to watch is something special. Do drop by when you are in Numazu!

26.pr: A saison-style craft beer brewed with the famed spring water of Kitakata, Fukushima and organic lemons from Kure, Hiroshima!
26.aroma: Lemon. Squeeze a few drops of lemon into it for a change of flavour!
26.pour: Pour it however you like! A few drops of fresh lemon in the beer changes the flavour!
26.story: Platanus Brewing is a brewery from Kure, Hiroshima. As a phantom brewery without equipment of its own, we work with partner breweries to plan and sell distinctive beers that draw on local ingredients and stories. With the concept of “rebuilding luxury”, we carefully design not just the taste but the aroma, the packaging and the moment of drinking, proposing a new craft beer experience that brings a little luxury and breathing room into everyday life.
26.trivia: New from Platanus Brewing: “Day Crisp”, a wheat ale that pairs the spiciness of Belgian wit yeast with the fruity aroma of Huell Melon hops. Not too heavy, with a crisp mouthfeel. We deliberately read “Crisp”, the beer term for a clean, refreshing finish, as “Clip”. The collage art on the label was made by analogue collage artist Hasebe, and the word ties the beer’s clean finish to the “clip” of the cut-out collage, the handwork of art. A glass that promises the experience of a good beer will be a special moment clipped out of everyday life. It will be served at Tsukuba Craft Beer Fest in October, so come and try it!

27.pr: Our flagship beer, combining a variety of hops with saison yeast. Gold medal winner in the American-Belgo-Style Ale category at the World Beer Cup 2026.
27.aroma: White wine and white grape notes lead, intricately layered with tropical fruit, berries and citrus
27.pour: A wine-shaped glass, and pour a proper head
27.story: We are Nara Brewing, a brewery in Nara City that started brewing in June 2018. So that craft beer lovers and beginners alike can enjoy our beer, we brew a wide variety without being bound by categories or styles, under the motto “the joy of choosing a beer!”. From classic beers to beers you can enjoy like dessert, find your favourite among our wide lineup. This is our first time at Tsukuba Craft Beer Fest. Cheers!
27.region:
Nara Brewing regularly makes beers with ingredients unique to Nara, such as PHILHARMONY with Yamato tachibana citrus and lemongrass, and EIGHTY EIGHT steeped with Yamato tea,
but our ties with the region go beyond ingredients.
We actively collaborate with other industries, such as the local sock maker HOiSUM and chef Kawashima of Acordu, one of Nara’s leading gastronomic restaurants.
Creating new value together with the many people active in Nara, not just making beer, is an important theme of our craft.
27.trivia:
Nara Brewing deliberately avoids designs that evoke Nara, such as deer or the Great Buddha.
Because beer travels beyond its region into many hands, we value original designs that make you want to pick it up.
The cat on the can label of our flagship FUNCTION: look closely at its eyes…???
It now appears on all sorts of merchandise, so keep an eye out!

28.pr: Made with barley grown in Oyama. Enjoy a fruity, grassy aroma with solid bitterness!
28.pour: Ice cold, no head, in your favourite glass
28.story: In Oyama, Tochigi we value “Drink Local”, using locally grown ingredients in our regular beers. Our limited beers span every style, with the goal of giving your everyday life “a choice of beer!”
28.region: We use ingredients grown in Oyama so that not only craft beer fans but the people of Oyama can discover craft beer, and so that others can discover Oyama.
28.trivia: Whatever the beer, we aim for a clean build.

29.style: Pale Ale w/ Local Red Pine needle
29.pr: “Nature” is one of the themes within our motto, Brew a better life. This is a forest-scented beer steeped with red pine needles gathered from the mountains of the Ina Valley.
29.aroma: Steeped with freshly gathered red pine needles and cones, so you can enjoy a fresh forest aroma.
29.pour: In your favourite glass. A wooden masu cup might bring out the woody aroma even more.
29.story: Back in Tsukuba after two years, from the Ina Valley in Shinshu. Enjoy a glass packed with the character of the Ina Valley that lets you feel our philosophy, Brew a better life. This year we are also planning to serve “beer yeast oyaki” dumplings in collaboration with the local oyaki shop Oyaki-dake. Look forward to pairing craft beer with oyaki!
29.region:
Our philosophy is “Brew a better life: a better life brews a better life”, and we make products around four themes: history and culture, people, nature and farming.
We believe these four themes make our daily lives better, and that living that way brews a good life.
One of the definitions of craft beer in the USA, where the culture began, is engagement with the local community, and that matches our philosophy and what we hold dear.
We have made beers themed on local history and culture taught to us by local people, using the traditional Shibihira nanban chilli,
and beers themed on environmental issues, using red pine at risk of pine wilt.
All of this carries our hope that people will not only get to know our region through our products, but also engage with and respect the history and culture of their own regions, learn about local issues, and think about their own way of living.
29.trivia:
Mori no Za, made with red pine from the Ina Valley, is on the menu at this event.
It actually had a predecessor, a prototype beer.
That one was based on a piney (pine resin) IPA with red pine added, and it truly divided opinion.
When we delivered it to a craft beer shop we were told “this is just too piney, it’s not good!”,
while some of our fans to this day say “the prototype was the best!”.
In the end, the current recipe is a pale ale base with minimal hops, so the fresh aroma of red pine stands out.
Mori no Za is also sold in cans, and the packaging uses real red pine.
It is kyogi, a rare material today: wood sliced paper-thin and applied by hand, sheet by sheet.
Each piece of red pine is cut and applied individually, so no two cans are the same.
If you get hold of one, why not peel the label off and see?

30.pr: Clean hop bitterness within the malt sweetness that comes from triple decoction. A classic pilsner born in the Czech lands.
30.aroma: Sweet malt flavour with the delicate, elegant aroma of European hops, herbal and floral
30.food: Fries, fried chicken, grilled scallop skewers and so on
30.pour: A tall glass, poured cold with a creamy head
30.story: A back-alley brewery restaurant in Kitasenju, a downtown district that has thrived as a post town since the Edo period. In a place that sits right beside everyday life in this lively town, we brew every day hoping to add a little colour to the ordinary. What we value most is the “free enjoyment” we see as craft beer’s greatest appeal. Beyond chasing deliciousness, we care about seasonality, variety and food pairing, aiming for beer that brings a smile the moment you taste it, and a place you want to visit every day.
30.region: We arrived as complete outsiders, but once we set up shop and started trading, it was striking how many locals took an interest. Ten years on from founding, people tell us “thank you for opening in Kitasenju, we’re proud to have you here”, and it really is a warm town. Perhaps it is the character of Kitasenju itself, a post town that has welcomed travellers since long ago.

31.story: Tokoshie Brewing was born in Ryugasaki, Ibaraki in December 2025. Our head brewer, with around ten years of experience, brews beers that pursue a clarity that clears your view as it passes your throat, and a comfort that lasts to the very last drop.
31.region:
Tokoshie Brewing values local production and giving back to the community. Not in every beer, but in some, we actively use rice and fresh fruit grown with care by local farmers as adjuncts.
On the way to our taproom you can see beautiful rice fields spreading out, and crops from those very fields go into some of our beers.
We value the experience of tasting with all five senses: “the scenery I just saw, I am tasting right here, right now”.
With the faces of the producers and the rich nature of this land in mind, we keep taking on special flavours that only Tokoshie Brewing can make.
31.trivia:
Our name, Tokoshie, means “eternity” in Japanese, and it carries two main wishes.
One is for the region: “may this beautiful farmland and the smiles of the people here continue forever into the future”.
The other is our passion for the craft: “because there is never a final answer in brewing, we want to be a brewery that keeps challenging itself and evolving forever”.

32.pr: Explosive citrus hop aroma, firm bitterness and malt in the best possible balance!
32.aroma: Citrus-led, with grapefruit and tangerine, and recent batches have picked up a dank note too.
32.story:
We brew in Numazu and Mishima, Shizuoka!
Sustainable brewing using solar power and groundwater, with around 50 beers a year.
From classics to the latest styles, we deliver new discoveries you won’t find anywhere else.
32.region:
Spent malt from brewing goes to local farmers as fertiliser, and through the Shizuoka cooperative it is also collected to be turned into feed.
Beyond our own open-brewery events, we hold events at the brewery together with the local young people’s association, deepening ties with the community.
32.trivia:
RePuBrew may be known for hoppy, showy IPAs and high-ABV beers, but we actually love classics too.
Last year a Helles and a Kölsch, before that an Alt, this year a Dortmunder: brewing dead-straight classics is RePuBrew too.
We treasure the classics while creating something new. Come and taste RePu’s classic side too.

1.look: A small, round body made of foam, with a cloud of pale gold bubbles on its head and a single young hop leaf tucked in. Slightly rosy cheeks.
1.persona: Laid-back and never shy. Never dismisses what you like, just gives you a gentle nudge.
1.home: Near the entrance, around the first booth
1.zukan: A light body like newborn foam that fades in a moment. Usually found near the festival entrance, gently guiding anyone who is undecided to the first tap. They say it has the potential to grow into any type.
ability: Eases the nerves of anyone nearby, making the first beer easy to choose.
moves: Leads anyone who is dithering to the first tap
Cleans the palate after a heavy beer
lines: “Clean” is a compliment, you know~
Another light one? Or a little adventure this time?
1.trivia: The first entry in the guide. With rival No.16, it’s “the first beer” versus “the last beer”.
1.neta: Beer trivia vanishes with the foam~

2.look: Slim and quick. Wears a cape like orange and lemon peel, with an aroma-catching net on its back. Its big nose is always twitching.
2.persona: Pure curiosity, never sits still. Finds a new aroma and forgets every plan.
2.home: Always on the move. Frequently spotted at session IPA taps
2.zukan: Races around the whole festival on a light body, stopping wherever a tap smells bold and fruity. They say its cape grows brighter with every aroma it has chased. A soft touch who shares every aroma caught in its net with friends right away.
ability: Can sniff out citrusy hop aroma from far away.
moves: Sprints toward wherever the aroma is
Pinpoints exactly what the aroma is
Links light beers one after another
lines: Hey, doesn’t this smell like grapefruit?
Light body, full-on aroma. That’s the whole point!
2.trivia: Keeps chasing rival Dark Meister around because the coffee aroma of dark beer is just too interesting.
2.neta: No aroma? Then I’m just passing through

3.look: A straight, sharp silhouette. A clear golden body with a headband of fine bubbles, and a pilsner glass carried on its back like a sword sheath.
3.persona: Quiet and cool. Hates waste. Gets a little bashful when told “that’s nicely chilled”.
3.home: Near the chillers, in the shade with a good breeze
3.zukan: Never wastes a single movement. Waits perfectly still inside a well-chilled glass, then flashes a sharp bitterness in the instant of the first sip. The sight of a sweating glass brings the faintest smile.
ability: The colder it gets, the stronger it becomes.
moves: A flash of sharp bitterness on the very first sip
Erases the aftertaste in an instant
Waits at low temperature, storing up power
lines: The aroma’s fine. What’s missing is the cold
…One more. Same again
3.trivia: Hates being told “drink more slowly” by rival Malt Dandy. Still drinks the water that gets handed over, though.
3.neta: Warm beer and small talk: I cut both

4.look: Hair spiked up like hop cones. Wears a green biker jacket and cradles a hop vine instead of a guitar.
4.persona: High energy and hot-blooded. Gets hyped faster than anyone when hop harvest comes around.
4.home: Near the stage, in front of the fresh hop taps
4.dislike: Places that are too quiet, beer that has lost its aroma
4.zukan: Hits peak hype when showered in the aroma of freshly harvested hops. A light body, yet it shakes the whole stage with aroma and bitterness. Sightings at beer festivals everywhere spike in autumn.
ability: Every stat goes up when showered in fresh hop aroma.
moves: Strums out aroma and gets the crowd going
A limited move, only usable during hop harvest
4.kime: Heard this year’s fresh hops yet?
lines: Aroma is something you listen to!
Encore? Of course, one more!
4.trivia: October at TCBF is fresh hop season. The festival lands in the most energetic time of the year.
4.neta: A mellow beer? Can’t hear it, the volume’s too low

5.look: A plump, round, straw-coloured body in an apron, collecting drops of golden foam in a little basket.
5.persona: Calm and meticulous. Treasures days that stay the same.
5.home: Near the rest benches, in front of the Helles tap
5.zukan: Builds a nest from golden foam gathered bit by bit. Pays no attention to flashy aromas, carefully choosing only beers that can be drunk every day. The nest smells faintly of fresh-baked bread.
ability: Tastes just as good on the fifth glass as the first.
moves: Calms the room with gentle malt sweetness
Collects favourite beers and keeps them safe
Recovers a little energy every day
5.kuchiguse: The usual is the best, isn’t it
5.kime: It doesn’t have to be fancy. I want to drink it every day
lines: Today’s beer is properly delicious too, isn’t it
I’ll add that one to my collection
5.trivia: Secretly admired by rival Hop Swordmaster, who says “I could never match that calm.”
5.neta: I’ll leave the adventures to someone else, thanks

6.look: A cloudy white, fluffy body. Ears shaped like ears of wheat, with a banana-yellow ribbon.
6.persona: Easygoing and a bit clingy. But never backs down when it comes to aroma.
6.home: In front of the wheat beer taps, on a sunny patch of grass
6.zukan: Said to be born from a breeze over a wheat field. Without leaning on hops, it spreads banana and clove aromas using yeast alone. Its hazy body is proof of its softness.
ability: Wrapped in the sweet aroma of yeast, it softens everyone’s mood.
moves: Wraps you in a fluffy mouthfeel
Makes yeast aroma blossom like a flower
6.kime: Aroma can bloom without any hops, you know
lines: Cloudy means it’s packed with flavour
Bitter isn’t really my thing… but I won’t give up the aroma
6.trivia: Complains that rival Classic Bitter is “way too bitter”, but secretly respects how steady it is.
6.neta: Life is bitter enough already, thanks

7.look: A slender body wrapped in a black robe, with a brooch of creamy foam on the chest. Carries a lantern shaped like a coffee bean.
7.persona: Polite and quiet. Secretly pleased when people are surprised.
7.home: The roastery at night, the dark beer tap at the edge of the festival
7.dislike: The assumption that dark beer means heavy beer
7.zukan: Anyone who sees the black body and expects something heavy is usually surprised. Patrols the roastery at night, quietly guarding a coffee-like roastiness and a finish that fades in a breath.
ability: A black body, yet the aftertaste vanishes in a breath.
moves: Keeps a quiet watch over the night with roasted aroma
Wraps the mouthfeel in smooth foam
Leaves just a trace of aroma after the last sip
7.kime: Dark doesn’t always mean heavy, you know
lines: My job is to guard the last breath of every glass
Surprised? …Then I’m glad
7.trivia: Dark Meister’s junior apprentice. With rival Juicy Collector it’s “clear jet black” versus “hazy gold”.
7.neta: Anyone who judges weight by colour gets surprised first

8.look: An antenna shaped like a tuning fork. Little bottles of herbs and spices hang from its body, and a thin wisp of smoke rises from its shoulders.
8.persona: A craftsman at heart, obsessive about detail. Notices the tiniest difference.
8.home: A farmhouse barn, the saison and spice ale taps
8.food: Smoked cheese, herb dishes, spiced curry
8.zukan: Herbs, spice, smoke, yeast. Has the ear to pick out these scattered notes and bring them into tune inside a single glass. Knows that aroma can play an ensemble even without the big sound of hops.
ability: Can pick out herb, spice and smoke aromas one by one.
moves: Lets smoky aroma ring out as the bass line
Keeps tempo with the dry finish of saison yeast
Balances the aromas to match your taste
8.kime: Smoke is the bass, herbs are the treble. See? It’s an ensemble
lines: You can’t fool my ears
Today’s beer is a semitone sharp, I’d say
8.trivia: Rival Rich Relaxer says “you overthink it~”, but always keeps the seat next door free.
8.neta: “Regular beer”? Which key is that in?

9.look: A big, stocky, amber-coloured body. Sleepy eyes, always hugging a small cushion.
9.persona: Easygoing and caring. Doesn’t like being rushed.
9.home: A bench with a view of the sunset
9.food: Roast beef, meat pie, cheddar cheese
9.zukan: Has a warm amber body, and time slows down just by being nearby. Not fond of flashy aromas, but fussier than anyone about the balance of malt and hops. Strongest at dusk.
ability: Slows down time for everyone around.
moves: Calms the room with the amber of dusk
Settles malt and hops into just the right balance
9.kime: No rush, no rush. The beer isn’t going anywhere
lines: I just love this amber colour
Not flashy, but just right, isn’t it?
9.trivia: Tells rival Flavor Tuner “you overthink it~”, yet always sits down right next to it.
9.neta: Speed-drinking contest? The participation prize is a hangover~

10.look: A plump, round body of hazy gold, like golden mist. Little mangoes and pineapples grow on its head.
10.persona: Sociable and trend-savvy. Loves new things and records everything.
10.home: The hazy IPA tap with the long queue
10.food: Spicy Thai food, a fruit platter
10.dislike: Old beer that has lost its aroma
10.zukan: A thick, rich body holding a swirl of tropical fruit aroma. They say that every new aroma it meets gets planted and raised in the orchard inside it.
moves: Wraps you in a swirl of aroma
Releases a thick burst of juiciness all at once
Records every aroma it meets, without missing one
10.kime: Can I plant that aroma in my orchard?
lines: Hazy? That’s a compliment
Aroma is all about freshness. Drink it while it’s new!
10.trivia: Swaps aroma intel with Fruity Hunter. Rival Afterglow Keeper is its complete opposite in looks and aroma.
10.neta: Hazy? Maybe you just haven’t caught up with the trend

11.look: A sturdy build in a well-worn leather vest. A white beard of foam, and an old hop sack slung over one shoulder.
11.persona: Stubborn and old-fashioned. Sharp-tongued but takes care of people.
11.home: A harbour pub, the old-style IPA tap
11.dislike: Beer that is too sweet, trendy buzzwords
11.zukan: A stubborn one that guards old-fashioned bitterness no matter how trends change. Has no taste for dressing up with aroma, competing on straight bitterness alone. Many young hops look up to it.
ability: The bitterness never changes, whatever the trend.
moves: Takes you on head-first with straight bitterness
Stubbornly keeps to the traditional way
11.kime: Beer is meant to be bitter, lad
lines: Back in my day, THIS was what IPA meant
Hazy, is it? …Fine, I’ll take one sip
11.trivia: Shares silent toasts with Crisp Master. Every time rival Soft Aromatist says “too bitter”, it seriously wonders whether to ease off a little.
11.neta: I don’t chase trends. They come back around on their own

12.look: Looks like an armoured warrior. A deep golden body with a helmet of white foam, and two swords made of hop cones at the hips.
12.persona: Bold and straightforward. Loves a contest, but always shows respect.
12.home: The dojo, the double IPA tap
12.food: Spare ribs, spicy chicken, aged cheese
12.zukan: A swordmaster carrying many times the usual hops in both hands. Its all-out strike of aroma, bitterness and body lingers long on the tongue of anyone who takes it. They say the stronger the opponent, the more it burns.
ability: Aroma, bitterness and body all hit maximum.
moves: Unleashes aroma and bitterness at once with two swords
Takes on any opponent with a heavy body
A combo move that layers hops twice
12.kime: Holding back would be an insult to the hops
lines: It is strong, so savour it sip by sip
Magnificent bitterness. Well done!
12.trivia: In the “Full-On Hop Alliance” with Hop Rocker. Secretly envies the calm of rival Mellow Collector.
12.neta: The words “hold back” have been painted over with hops

13.look: A deep amber to brown body. A long beard made of ears of barley, little round glasses and a thick book.
13.persona: Thoughtful and well-read. Talks a little too long.
13.home: The library, a quiet corner of the festival
13.zukan: Sits for hours in front of a single bock, deep in thought. Can read the story of where the malt was grown and how it was roasted from its sweetness alone. Says little, but once it starts, it cannot stop.
ability: Reads how the malt was grown and roasted from its sweetness.
moves: Focuses deeply, deeply on malt sweetness
Doubles up its thinking to reach the answer
Wraps everyone in a sweet caramel aroma
13.kuchiguse: Hmm… where does this sweetness come from
13.kime: To know malt is to know oneself
lines: In my view, beer is time
No need to rush an answer. The glass is still half full
13.trivia: Complains that rival Hop Rocker’s music is too loud to think, yet goes to the show every single year.
13.neta: Malt does not speak to those who order “whatever”

14.look: A deep reddish-brown body in a top hat and waistcoat. Carries a pocket watch, with raisins in the breast pocket.
14.persona: Gentlemanly and unhurried. Attentive to everyone around.
14.home: The lounge, the taps with the stronger beers
14.zukan: A gentleman of great poise, wrapped in the aroma of raisins and caramel. Tilts a strong beer slowly from a small glass. Quietly offers a glass of water to anyone drinking too fast.
ability: Can enjoy a rich beer even after a full meal.
moves: Takes its time and savours slowly
Offers water to look after you
14.kuchiguse: Oh, do have some water too
14.kime: A hurried glass holds no afterglow
lines: I shall take mine in a small glass
A piece of chocolate, if you like
14.trivia: Always nervous about how fast rival Crisp Master drinks. Still offers water every time.
14.neta: Chugging, you say. I’ll bring extra water

15.look: A body like jet-black armour with a black leather apron. Shoulders plated in roasted malt, and only its eyes glow amber.
15.persona: A craftsman of few words. Speaks through the beer, not words. Looks after the juniors.
15.home: The workshop, the stout and porter taps
15.zukan: Clad in black armour made of deeply roasted malt. A craftsman who speaks through the beer rather than words. Fans never stop admiring how it wears dark beer like a suit.
ability: Armoured in roast, it stands up to even the richest food.
moves: Hits hard with a heavy body
15.kime: Black takes on no other colour
lines: ……Good? Then that’s all that matters
Roasting leaves nowhere to hide
15.trivia: Afterglow Keeper’s senior. Troubled by rival Fruity Hunter chasing it around, but a little pleased when the coffee aroma gets praised.
15.neta: ……Say whether it’s good after you drink it

16.look: Sits on a great barrel as a throne. A body patterned like tree rings, a cloak of smoke, and deep amber eyes.
16.persona: Dignified, yet very kind to anyone who makes it this far.
16.home: The far end of the festival, the ageing cellar
16.food: Smoked salmon, dark chocolate, aged cheese
16.zukan: A legendary presence living at the deepest point of the craft beer rabbit hole. Sleeps long inside a barrel, and each time it wakes, its aroma and bitterness have deepened. They say it is only seen at the last beer of the festival.
ability: Aroma and bitterness grow deeper as time passes.
moves: A grand move that releases smoky aroma
Sleeps inside a barrel, storing up power
Appears only at the close of the festival
16.kuchiguse: Well done making it this far
16.kime: Share the last beer with me
lines: I am in no hurry. I waited years inside a barrel
A strong one. Share it with friends and savour it
16.trivia: Some say rival Gentle Starter is actually what the Legend looked like when young. Late-night conversation partner of Malt Dandy.
16.neta: I have never met anyone who left after the first beer

friends: Bitterness fans who toast in silence
Senior and junior of the dark beer school
rivals: The first beer and the last beer
The speed of one sip versus a slow afterglow
A loud live show versus quiet contemplation
Clear jet black versus hazy gold
An ensemble of character versus classic comfort

story.t: Cover: How Does That Beer Reach You?
story.x: TCBF2026 × Tsukuba University of Technology. How does that beer reach you? The making of Beer meets Design.
My job is to pick the one track that fits everyone on the floor, and deliver it. Today, let me tell you the story of how beer met design.

About 40 breweries, over 200 craft beers. TCBF is a festival that university students started in 2011. This year, the 13th, over 200 craft beers will be lined up. The theme is “beer meets ____”. It’s the year beer meets something new.
But you can only drink a few glasses a day. Not knowing the difference, plenty of people choose by the length of the queue or by “whatever”.

Every brewery has its own passion and story. And yet people walk past before they ever meet it. What’s missing is the way that appeal gets across. “Even a great track won’t make anyone dance if it doesn’t reach them.”

story.t: If it’s about getting across, ask those people.
story.x: We wanted every brewery to have a chance to be discovered. So we asked people who think about how things get across. We visited Tsukuba University of Technology, where students study design while facing differences in how people see and hear.

story.t: The question we gave the students
story.x: Out of about 40 breweries, how do we help each visitor meet “the beer that fits them”? Theme: “Meet it before you drink. Notice it after.” Ideas that reach touch and scent, not just the eyes, were welcome too.

The students presented one by one and talked with 22 judges from companies, Tsukuba City and universities. Questions and comments were also shared as text on screen. Whatever their hearing, everyone could talk while looking at the same information. The text was shared with Tsukuba University of Technology’s “ISeee TimeLine”.

The first: learn your taste type, and meet the opposite of what you like too. The second: cute characters that welcome first-timers. The third: meet beer through food, with pictures and English that cross the language barrier.

story.t: The chosen ideas come to the festival.
story.x: The students’ ideas become real at TCBF2026. Take the Beer Type Quiz: answer 8 questions and find your beer personality among 16 types. It also suggests a beer close to your type from 32 breweries.

What the students dreamed up is waiting for you at the festival. Once you know your type, try “the beer that fits” and “its complete opposite” side by side. Change how it gets across, and you change who meets whom. Enjoy every minute! Take the quiz on your phone any time. October 16 (Fri) to 18 (Sun), 2026, Tsukuba Center Plaza.

beer meets Design / Tsukuba Craft Beer Fest 2026. Organised by the Tsukuba Craft Beer Fest Executive Committee, co-organised by Tsukuba Machinaka Design Co., Ltd., with the cooperation of Tsukuba City and the Tsukuba Center District Revitalisation Council. Thinking alongside us: the students of Tsukuba University of Technology. tsukuba-craftbeerfest.com
